title: Incremental topical-slab sampler with weighted exemplar anchoring for calibration slices
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Goal: produce deterministic, production-representative micro-slices used to calibrate FP8/INT8 quantization profiles while minimizing sampling cost and preserving per-topic signal. We propose an incremental 'topical-slab' sampler that groups prompts into topic slabs (fine-grained clusters derived from embeddings and metadata), enforces per-slab quotas, anchors high-utility exemplars, and applies a tunable recency-decay multiplier. The sampler will emit compact calibration packs for each tenant/domain-like slab, preserving conversational context length distribution and response modalities (chat vs single-turn).
acceptance_criteria: Sampler produces labeled calibration slices (<= 2k prompts per slab) that match production topic distribution within +/-5% for top-10 topics
FP8 and INT8 calibration runs using new slices show no more than 1.5% relative degradation on per-slab evaluator compared to full-sample baseline
End-to-end pipeline (extract -> cluster -> sample -> dedupe -> pack) can run incremental daily and produce differential packs in < 90 minutes for seed tenant dataset (~5M prompts/day)
Automated validation harness compares new pack vs baseline and emits a regression alert to console-qa dashboard when regressions exceed threshold
comments: 2025-01-15 Marcus Chen: Initial proposal. Rationale: existing per-domain packs are coarse for multi-vertical tenants; topical slabs let us capture fine-grained signal (e.g., billing vs billing_disputes). Want to reduce calibration pack size while retaining coverage for FP8/INT8 sensitivity tests.

2025-01-18 Priya Nair: Spike results: baseline clustering (SBERT 768-d) yields 180 slabs for seed tenant; added fast KMedoids to stabilize cluster anchors. Observed that naive stratified sampling misses low-frequency but high-utility exemplars.

2025-01-22 Ava Reynolds (Design): UX note: sampling metadata should include 'anchor_reason' and 'topic_id' so that Console can surface pack explainability. We'll add compact metadata to pack manifest.

2025-01-24 Diego Alvarez (Eng): Implementation plan: 1) extractor lambda for rolling window, 2) incremental embed-store update, 3) slab-assignment microservice, 4) weighted-reservoir sampler with recency decay, 5) pack composer + dedupe. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/calibration-sampler/pull/189

2025-01-28 Priya Nair: Trade-offs discussed with Research. We bias anchors by a combined utility score (impact_score = traffic_weight * failure_rate_score + manual_priority). This increases recall for regression-sensitive prompts but skew overall topic frequency; to compensate we cap anchor fraction to 12% of each slab pack.

2025-01-30 Marcus Chen: Added validation plan. Use existing quant-val harness (https://internal.redwood/dashboards/quant-val) to run A/B: baseline full-sample vs topical-slab packs across FP8/INT8 quant profiles. Metrics: token-KL, n-gram overlap (BLEU/Rouge-L for instr prompts), and API-level correctness (task-specific scoring).

2025-02-02 Priya Nair: Prototype run completed for tenant 'acme-marketing' (5M daily prompts): produced 210 topical slabs; average pack size 1.2k; sampling pipeline latency 62 minutes. Observed FP8 calibration: mean KL increase 0.9% vs baseline, max per-slab 1.3% — within target. Preparing design doc and rollout checklist.

technical_notes: Clustering: two-stage (coarse L2 kmeans on PCA -> fine HDBSCAN on reduced embeddings) to avoid topic drift and produce stable slab IDs
Anchors: select top-K exemplars per slab by impact_score; ensure diversity by enforcing token-length bucket constraints (short/medium/long)
Recency decay: exponential decay factor lambda configurable per-tenant; default lambda=0.97/day to favor recent signals while preserving long-tail
Dedupe: cross-slab fuzzy-hash dedupe to avoid identical prompts across packs; maintain original request_id mapping for audit
Serializer: pack manifest is newline-delimited JSONL with minimal fields: prompt_id, slab_id, anchor_reason, sampling_weight, original_ts
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (dev): run prototype on one non-prod tenant; validate performance and pack stability
Stage 1 (canary): run nightly for 3 production tenants; run quant-val A/B and monitor per-slab regressions
Stage 2 (gradual): enable for all tenants with tenant-level knobs (anchor_fraction, slab_quota, lambda)
Stage 3 (GA): document in runbook, add Console toggles for pack generation and on-demand re-run
metrics: Per-slab task accuracy delta (tenant eval set)
Anchor coverage (% of high-impact prompts included)
